general.temas: Education protests and tensions in schools feature in Le Figaro, Libération and Le Parisien. Other recurring stories include the presence of French troops in Ukraine, Gérard Depardieu’s conviction, the court case involving Gims, the controversy surrounding «Le Masque et la Plume» and Philippe Diallo’s possible bid for the FIFA presidency. Only Ouest-France highlights the discovery of a new fossil fish species.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions are considerable amid protests by teachers, students and unions demanding more resources and pay rises from the government. The education minister’s turbulent visit to Nantes and restrictions on some gatherings reflect tensions around schools. Violence as a political marker and international confrontations linked to Ukraine also feature prominently. Stories about health, sport and scientific discoveries provide a calmer counterpoint.

Le Monde.resumen:
- Violence emerges as a key political factor in France; the paper also examines the loss of purchasing power ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
- Small French military contingents are operating in Ukraine, while Gulf countries plan more underground infrastructure in response to drone attacks.
- Gérard Depardieu has decided not to appeal his conviction for sexual assault; Nathalie Roret has been appointed children’s rights defender.
- A report links artificial intelligence to climate disinformation, while India is developing its own model through the company Sarvam.
- Municipal elections will be rerun in Wittelsheim; the paper also reports the deaths of Julien Laroche-Joubert and former mayor Michel Destot.
Le Monde.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual and restrained; expressions such as «French fractures» and «coup d’état» add drama, but the latter is attributed to opponents and there are no appeals to the people against the elites.
Le Monde.sesgo: The selection prioritises French politics and society, alongside international security and technology. It frequently draws on institutional sources and experts, with no clear partisan leaning apparent overall.

Le Figaro.resumen:
- The education minister’s visit to a secondary school in Nantes takes place amid tensions, as teachers and students prepare further protests.
- A public-sector strike calls for pay rises; demonstrations and possible disruption to transport are expected.
- The government temporarily suspends the sale of certain pyrotechnic items, and police arrest four people suspected of trying to set fire to a secondary school.
- France is providing military support to Ukraine, the EU is imposing new sanctions on Russia, Estonia is announcing the closure of its border with Russia and Germany is strengthening its intelligence services.
- The front page also covers the revival of the Ferrandaise cattle breed, a possible FIFA presidential bid by Philippe Diallo and a dispute over a cultural programme.
Le Figaro.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as «youth in flames», «chaotic visit» and «social anger» add drama, but factual headlines predominate and there is no clear appeal to the people against the elites.
Le Figaro.sesgo: The selection highlights social conflicts and security incidents, focusing on tensions and the authorities’ responses. War and external threats also dominate international coverage, with no unequivocal political leaning apparent.

Libération.resumen:
- A magistrate recounts her work with teenage victims of sexual exploitation in Melun.
- Rapper Gims will stand trial for alleged corruption; Gérard Depardieu apologises and gives up his appeal against his conviction for sexual assault.
- The front page follows the social protests in Paris and covers the dispute between four right-wing candidates.
- It examines China’s role in the energy transition and its opposition to new binding climate agreements.
- In culture, it reports warnings about cuts and possible restrictions on creative work, a controversy at France Inter and the launch of GTA VI.
Libération.motivo_populismo: Factual reporting predominates, but expressions such as «ego trip», «legal weapon» and «attack on freedom of expression» introduce disparagement and a combative tone, without a broader confrontation between the people and the elites.
Libération.sesgo: The selection prioritises social, judicial and cultural issues, with attention to artists’ precarious circumstances and possible restrictions on freedom of expression. In politics, one article directly addresses left-wing voters and criticises the rivalry between right-wing candidates.

Le Parisien.resumen:
- A wine merchant was targeted with an explosive device in Hérault; a radical group of producers claims responsibility.
- Inass Touloub’s siblings call for an end to the use of her photographs.
- The education minister was booed at a fire-damaged secondary school in Nantes; another headteacher faces accusations of toxic management.
- Several stories cover incidents, including a man found with cuts to his throat and arrests near a secondary school.
- The front page also covers suspicions surrounding rapper Gims, a dispute at a campsite, taxation of rental properties, Miss France and a survivor’s account.
Le Parisien.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as «little martyr», «moving account» and «showdown» add emotional weight and drama, although there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
Le Parisien.sesgo: The selection gives prominence to violent incidents, conflicts and personal stories, with some emotionally charged headlines. No defined political bias is apparent.

Ouest-France.resumen:
- Jensen Huang is reportedly preparing to return to Nvidia after resigning; some in Silicon Valley support him.
- Researchers recommend adapting older people’s diets to combat malnutrition.
- Crozon hosted an international foiling competition, a growing sport.
- An episode of «Demain nous appartient» will air with a warning for children under ten because of its violence.
- The front page includes several sports stories, a scooter accident in Le Mans and the discovery of a fossil in Saint-Étienne.
Ouest-France.motivo_populismo: The tone is predominantly factual, although expressions such as «Bring Jensen back!», «foiling revolution» and «zero chance» add emphasis; there is no apparent rhetoric pitting the people against the elites.
Ouest-France.sesgo: The selection gives particular weight to sport, alongside technology, health, television and local incident stories. No clear political bias is apparent.

opiniones.comunista:
I see the strike day as a clear expression of class struggle: those who sustain public services are demanding wages that allow them to live with dignity. If only the minimum wage is indexed to inflation, protecting the purchasing power of all workers must be a priority, not an exceptional concession.

The campaign for more resources for education raises the same question: for whose benefit is wealth organised? I stand for well-funded public schools and the right to demonstrate peacefully. I also reject leaving culture at the mercy of cuts. In the face of a model that concentrates economic decision-making in the hands of big capital, we need collective ownership and democratic control of strategic sectors: the wealth we all produce must serve our common needs.
opiniones.anarquista:
Today I see the same question behind the education protests and the strike over pay: who decides the conditions of our lives? Banning gatherings around some schools does not address the demands of those who study and work in them. In my view, it is not enough to wait for a political party to turn those demands into election promises, either.

I prefer organising from the bottom up: open assemblies, shared decisions and mutual support among teachers, students and workers. Individual freedom also needs that collective strength if it is not to be left at the mercy of bosses and governments.

I am equally concerned that the republican commitment contract is being used to obstruct support for artists considered subversive. A free culture should not depend on obedience to the authorities. Self-management does not eliminate conflicts, but it makes it possible to confront them without always leaving those in power with the final say.
opiniones.liberal:
I am concerned that violence is becoming a political marker. The freedom to demonstrate deserves protection, but it does not include setting fire to a school or threatening those who think differently. The state must guarantee security and enforce the law, without turning every protest into an excuse to restrict rights.

I understand public-sector workers demanding better pay. But increasing spending is not an automatic answer: someone has to pay for it. I prefer a limited state that assesses its priorities, reduces the tax burden and leaves more room for private enterprise. A freer, more competitive economy offers better prospects for raising wages sustainably than a succession of tax-funded promises.

Responsibility is also individual: defending a cause does not exempt us from answering for our actions.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
In today’s news, I see a France that needs to regain a sense of its priorities. The fire at a secondary school in Nantes and the arrests near another in Bagnolet are reminders that authority is not restored through statements alone. Defending schools means protecting pupils and teachers, punishing offences and instilling respect for the rules, without confusing those who demonstrate peacefully with those who resort to violence.

Meanwhile, French troops are operating in Ukraine. Before expanding any commitment, I want a clear public debate about its risks and the national interest. Sovereignty also means that our leaders answer to the French people, not just to their partners. And the revival of the Ferrandaise breed reminds us that our rural traditions deserve more than speeches: they need continuity and support.
opiniones.centro:
I am concerned that violence is becoming a political marker. The campaign for pay and resources for education deserves to be heard; attacks on schools, by contrast, must be unequivocally rejected. Upholding the right to demonstrate and protecting pupils and teachers are not incompatible goals. I call on the government and unions to engage in serious negotiations, with gradual commitments and a clear explanation of how they will be funded: promising everything without saying how to pay for it only fuels distrust.

I also support French assistance to Ukraine to train personnel and repair equipment. But support abroad requires democratic oversight and public explanations of its objectives and risks. Firmness does not require us to abandon debate; on the contrary, institutions gain legitimacy when they justify their decisions and agree to be held accountable.
